about: Reviewed allow-list for scripts/vsix-scan.mjs (docs/DESIGN.md#rules). Each entry names one hit by file (path inside the VSIX), line, the watched name or module, and the line's text; the scan fails if a hit is missing here, if an entry no longer matches a hit (the file changed: review it again), or if an entry tries to allow child_process (allowed only in extension/dist/fork.js, by rule, not by this list).

The entries for pdf.js's files are in pdf.js (pdfjs-dist 6.4.299, Apache-2.0), copied verbatim. pdf.js runs only inside the viewer webview. Its Content Security Policy is default-src 'none' with connect-src limited to webview.cspSource, so these calls can reach only the extension's own files, and the extension gives pdf.js each PDF as bytes, never as a URL.

Entries for extension/dist/engine/engine.js apply to a package built with --with-engine or --test-copy; each is pinned to the glue's line and text, and the glue itself to its SHA-256 (engine/pins.json, checked by the scan). An entry whose file is not in the VSIX is not checked.

entries.reason: fetchData(): the page's loader for the cMap, standard-font and WASM files under the in-extension cMapUrl, standardFontDataUrl and wasmUrl. The viewer runs pdf.js with useWorkerFetch off, so this is the path those files take (S3).
fetchData()'s XMLHttpRequest fallback for URLs fetch() cannot take; same files as the entry above.
A constant read (XMLHttpRequest.DONE) inside the same fallback.
PDFFetchStream: loads a PDF given by URL. The viewer passes getDocument({ data }), never a url, so this path does not run.
PDFNetworkStream: range requests for a PDF given by URL; does not run, as above.
fetchBinaryData(): the worker's own loader, used only with useWorkerFetch on; the viewer turns it off because a blob: worker cannot load webview resources in VS Code (S3).
wasm-bindgen's loader in the qcms colour module, used only when given a path; pdf.js calls initSync() with bytes it loaded from wasmUrl.
fetchSync(): the worker's synchronous load of qcms_bg.wasm and the CMYK ICC profile, used only with useWorkerFetch on (off in the viewer).
Emscripten's readAsync in the JBIG2 decoder glue; pdf.js hands the decoder its WASM bytes itself, so this is not called.
Emscripten's readAsync in the OpenJPEG decoder glue; not called, as above.

the engine glue (engine.js, Emscripten 6.0.13's own output, unpatched; SHA-256 4fc08dd4c837334afa553951a66dc914dfcf0a95f9631310aeb505d40920dceb, pinned in engine/pins.json): instantiateAsync's streaming path, behind "!binary && !ENVIRONMENT_IS_NODE". The engine host runs under Node and passes its compiled module through instantiateWasm, so the glue never fetches the wasm.

the engine glue (engine.js, Emscripten 6.0.13's own output, unpatched; SHA-256 4fc08dd4c837334afa553951a66dc914dfcf0a95f9631310aeb505d40920dceb, pinned in engine/pins.json): FS.forceLoadFile, which runs only for a lazy file (one made by FS.createLazyFile). In a browser worker it aborts; under Node, which has no XMLHttpRequest, its else branch would read the lazy file's URL from the real disk (readBinary, fs.readFileSync). The engine never makes a lazy file: the host mounts the data images as LZ4 nodes and writes the project with FS.writeFile, and ESLint refuses createLazyFile and preloadFile in src/.

the engine glue (engine.js, Emscripten 6.0.13's own output, unpatched; SHA-256 4fc08dd4c837334afa553951a66dc914dfcf0a95f9631310aeb505d40920dceb, pinned in engine/pins.json): FS.createLazyFile's length probe (a synchronous HEAD request for a lazy file). The engine creates no lazy file, so this is never reached.

the engine glue (engine.js, Emscripten 6.0.13's own output, unpatched; SHA-256 4fc08dd4c837334afa553951a66dc914dfcf0a95f9631310aeb505d40920dceb, pinned in engine/pins.json): FS.createLazyFile's range reader (a synchronous GET for a lazy file). The engine creates no lazy file, so this is never reached.

the engine glue (engine.js, Emscripten 6.0.13's own output, unpatched; SHA-256 4fc08dd4c837334afa553951a66dc914dfcf0a95f9631310aeb505d40920dceb, pinned in engine/pins.json): FS.createLazyFile's check for a browser worker; under Node, which has no XMLHttpRequest, it takes the other branch. The engine never makes a lazy file (ESLint refuses createLazyFile and preloadFile in src/), so neither branch is reached.
